# Meaning as a cognitive representation

I study the cognitive representations that underlie linguistic meaning: the format and structure they take, how they are constructed from linguistic input and context, how they are accessed and used in inference, and how they are retained in memory.

My work combines linguistic theory and experimental psycholinguistics because **theories of representation and theories of processing constrain one another**.

## How does the mind construct and use meaning?

<p class="research-intro">I use linguistic theory to formulate precise hypotheses about meaningful representations, and experimental psycholinguistics to investigate how those representations are built and used. The three perspectives below are different entry points into the same problem.</p>
:::

<div class="section-kicker">Prospective researchers</div>

## DPhil students and postdocs

I am interested in working with researchers who want to investigate the cognitive representation of meaning, particularly where linguistic theory and experimental approaches can inform one another.

Projects might concern linguistic representation, incremental interpretation, inference and prediction, memory and knowledge, discourse, or related questions at the interface of language and cognition. A strong fit need not reproduce my existing projects; what matters is a well-specified question for which linguistic theory and experimental evidence can usefully constrain one another.

[Information about working with me →](people.html)
